The two weeks that matter

In Cobb County the straw goes down twice. Once for the spring HOA walk-throughs, once before Thanksgiving company arrives.

SPRING

Dogwoods and azaleas open, HOA walk-throughs start. We spread fresh long-leaf while the blooms are out so the beds read clean for the inspection.

Book spring
FALL

Oaks drop their leaves, family drives in for Thanksgiving. We clear the beds, recut the edge and put down a deep red-brown layer before company arrives.

Book fall

When will my straw look gray?

Sun or shade?

Top-up in August · Next full refresh: Fall

Put me on that week

Rake, edge, pull, spread, blow

  1. Rake the old out

    Faded straw and oak leaves pulled from the beds and hauled away.

  2. Cut the bed line

    A spade recuts the curve where the clay has crept into the lawn.

  3. Pull the weeds

    Hand-pulled before the new straw goes down so they do not come back through.

  4. Shake and tuck

    Long-leaf flakes shaken loose and tucked under the drip line, off the stems.

  5. Blow the walks

    Driveway, path and porch cleaned up before we leave.

If your HOA flags a bed we spread, we fix it before your deadline.

Red clay and long-leaf needles at a Cobb County bed edge.

What we do

  • Spring pine straw refresh

    New straw down when the dogwoods open, in time for spring HOA walk-throughs.

    Price it

  • Fall pine straw refresh

    Leaves cleared and beds topped off after the oaks drop, before Thanksgiving company.

    Price it

  • Pine straw installation

    Beds edged, weeded and covered in long-leaf straw over the red clay.

    Price it

  • HOA and common-area beds

    Entrance beds, islands and common areas done on one scheduled day per neighborhood.

    Price it

  • Leaf removal

    Oak and maple leaves blown from beds, lawn and walks, then hauled away.

    Price it

  • Shrub trimming

    Hollies, boxwoods and loropetalum cut back after bloom so the beds read clean.

    Price it

  • Bed edging

    Curved bed lines recut each season so the clay does not creep into the lawn.

    Price it

  • Annual programs

    Both refreshes booked a year ahead, same week each spring and each fall.

Sample pricing

Counted bales, not guesses

Long-leaf pine straw, edged and weeded. Prices below are sample ranges for typical Cobb front-and-back beds; your count comes from the estimator.

  • $7–$10 per bale · long-leaf, edged and weeded
  • $350–$700 · typical Cobb front and back beds
  • $650–$1,300 · spring and fall, booked ahead
  • $150–$450 · beds and lawn, hauled away
  • $900–$3,500 · entrances and islands, per visit
Get a number

Your exact bale count depends on bed square footage and depth. Tell us the beds or walk them with us and we price it to the bale.
